scenes.name: 01-dilemma
scenes.caption:
“I can’t tell my family what I want without feeling ungrateful.”
Fictional · prepared scenario.

scenes.name: 02-audience-and-path
scenes.caption:
For people navigating family pressure: clarify privately,
correct the reflection, then choose whether to share.

scenes.name: 03-private-choice
scenes.caption:
He chooses a private first step.
No one else sees this reflection.

scenes.name: 04-own-words
scenes.caption:
Arjun puts the family pressure into his own words.
He starts privately.

scenes.name: 05-planned-model-role
scenes.caption:
Planned Muse Spark role: suggest a tentative reflection
from words you choose to share; you decide whether it fits.

scenes.name: 06-prepared-result
scenes.caption: Prepared text · no model connected.

scenes.name: 07-possible-meaning
scenes.caption:
A possible meaning is offered
as something he can check.

scenes.name: 08-reject
scenes.caption:
He says “Not quite.”
The first interpretation does not stand.

scenes.name: 09-correction
scenes.caption:
He corrects it. He needs time to decide.
This time, he names what fits.

scenes.name: 10-changed-result
scenes.caption:
His correction changes the editable reflection.
The result now includes his words.

scenes.name: 11-confirmed-theme
scenes.caption:
He confirms the theme himself.
The product does not decide what is true.

scenes.name: 12-choice-to-explore
scenes.caption:
Only now does he choose
to hear other experiences.

scenes.name: 13-correction-changes-results
scenes.caption:
He sets aside broad legal results.
Family context stays in view.

scenes.name: 14-enter-community
scenes.caption:
He opens the family expectations
community preview.

scenes.name: 15-fiction-label
scenes.caption:
Prepared and fictional.
This is not a live community.

scenes.name: 16-peer-perspective
scenes.caption:
Ravi names a different path: a trusted friend
helped him speak with family.

scenes.name: 17-shared-pressure
scenes.caption:
They share family pressure,
but the circumstances differ.

scenes.name: 18-different-support
scenes.caption:
Ravi had someone he trusted.
Arjun has not said he does.

scenes.name: 19-group-only
scenes.caption:
Questions stay in the group,
never in a direct message.

scenes.name: 20-edited-question
scenes.caption:
He edits the question
to ask for time before answering.

scenes.name: 21-consent-boundary
scenes.caption:
Group and alias are shown.
Private reflection is excluded.

scenes.name: 22-cancel
scenes.caption:
He cancels.
Nothing is sent; the draft remains his.

scenes.name: 23-no-reply-yet
scenes.caption:
A later prepared thread has no reply yet.
A response is not promised.

scenes.name: 24-private-takeaway
scenes.caption:
Arjun keeps one takeaway privately
for this preview session.

scenes.name: 25-bounded-offer
scenes.caption:
He may offer one bounded thing
that helped to Dev’s example group.

scenes.name: 26-edit-and-review
scenes.caption:
He edits the exact contribution. Consent stays unchecked.
The local draft remains unsent.

scenes.name: 27-choice-end-state
scenes.caption:
Private takeaway kept.
Optional group contribution remains unposted.

checks.changedReflection: You want time to decide what you want, without someone choosing stay or leave for you.
checks.raviProvenance:
Illustrative experience · Ravi
Ravi

At first I asked everyone what I should do about my relationship. I got completely different answers. Some were kind, some felt like instructions. I stopped asking for a verdict and asked one trusted friend to listen while I worked out what mattered to me. I was still uncertain afterward, but I could hear my own thinking again.

One person's account, not a recommendation for your decision.

WHERE YOUR LIVES DIFFER
What may not carry over
